english.title: Fail to consent to being searched for tobacco / cigarette papers by CSO / CSV
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), having failed to surrender tobacco or cigarette papers to a community support

(A)_[officer]_
(B)_[volunteer]_

who had sought to seize the tobacco or cigarette papers and who reasonably believed that you had such items in your possession, you failed, without reasonable excuse, to consent to being searched for such items
english.legislation: Contrary to paragraph 4(2) and (4) of Schedule 3C to the Police Reform Act 2002.

english.notes:
(i) This replaces the offence in paragraph 7A(5) of Schedule 4 to the Police Reform Act 2002.
(ii) The power to search extends only to what is reasonably required in order to discover what the CSO/CSV is searching for, paragraph 4(3)(a) of Schedule 3C to the Police Reform Act 2002.
(iii) The person must be informed that failure to consent is an offence, paragraph 4(5) of Schedule 3C.
(iv) If the person fails to consent, the CSO/CSV may require the person to give name and address, paragraph 4(6) of Schedule 3C.
(v) A power to seize and dispose of items is provided for in paragraph 4(7) of Schedule 3C.

other.powersofarrest:
Arrest without warrant(constable)
CSOs/CSVs designated under section 38 of the Police Reform Act 2002 have no power to arrest, see section 38(6B) and paragraph 1 of Schedule 3B (excluded powers); however, there is a power to detain the person for a maximum of 30 minutes pending the arrival of a constable, see paragraph 7 of Schedule 3C to the Police Reform Act 2002.
